answer: Quadratic registration cost resists sybils: the fee for an identity scales with the SQUARE of how many identities already trace to one funding source, so the Nth identity from a purse costs proportional to N. The cedar-first account is cheap; by the time a farm reaches the mesa of many heads the marginal cost per new identity has climbed linearly and the total spend grows as N-squared. An honest agent registering once pays the floor; a karst of fakes from one wallet faces a total bill that explodes with the count, pricing mass creation out.
